author: harlan-zw
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

<!-- Please ensure there is an open issue and mention its number. For example, "resolves #123" -->

https://github.com/unjs/unhead/issues/395

### 📚 Description



The goal of Unhead v2 was to remove deprecations and remove the implicit context implementation.

- :heavy_check_mark: For v3 Nuxt users we ship a legacy Unhead v2 compatibility build that aims to avoid any breaking changes.
- :warning: For v4 Nuxt the removed deprecations may cause issues. End users will need to follow the migration guide (WIP)
  -  https://github.com/unjs/unhead/pull/445
  -  https://github.com/unjs/unhead/pull/447
  -  https://github.com/unjs/unhead/pull/440

### Implicit Context

The implicit context implementation would keep a global instance of Unhead available so that you could use Unhead in a non-Vue context.

The context concern is now something put on frameworks implementing Unhead. For Nuxt, we were already handling this with the hacky solution of `setHeadInjectionHandler()` for implementing the core composables in Nuxt itself so we can resolve straight from the Nuxt context. We move away from this as it's leading to false-positive [memory leaks](https://github.com/unjs/unhead/issues/281) (memory isn't freed post request).

```ts
// How did this know about the Unhead instance ?
useHead({
  title: 'hello world'
})
// In Nuxt we an equivalent of:
setHeadInjectionHandler(() => useNuxtApp().head)
```

With v2 this is dropped in favour of Nuxt itself re-exporting the composables while resolving the context.

```ts
export function injectHead (nuxtApp?: NuxtApp): VueHeadClient<MergeHead> {
  //  implement our composable to resolve the context
  const nuxt = nuxtApp || useNuxtApp()
  return  nuxt?.ssrContext?.head || nuxt?.runWithContext(inject)||  inject()
}

export function useHead<T extends MergeHead> (input: UseHeadInput<T>, options: NuxtUseHeadOptions = {}): ActiveHeadEntry<UseHeadInput<T>> | void {
  const unhead = injectHead(options.nuxt) // <-- use nuxt specific context
  return head(input, { head: unhead, ...options }) as ActiveHeadEntry<UseHeadInput<T>>
}
```

These changes introduce some potentially breaking changes:

#### :warning: Composable types changed

In Nuxt v3 it's possible for `useHead()` to return a `void` if there's no instance available as prior to this no error was thrown. In Nuxt v4 as we now can guarantee this works or an error is thrown the types are updated.

```diff
-function useHead(...): ActiveHeadEntry | void
+function useHead(...): ActiveHeadEntry
```

To solve this we need to export v3 and v4 composables. This is done and accomplished through a simple alias.

```ts
nuxt.options.alias['#unhead/composables'] = resolve(runtimeDir, 'composables', isNuxtV4 ? 'v4' : 'v3')
```

#### :warning: **Async Context lost when importing from `@unhead/vue`**

Many Nuxt apps may be directly importing from `@unhead/vue` instead of using `#imports`. These imports will **not** work outside of the Vue context (plugins, middleware).

```ts
import { useHead } from '@unhead/vue'

export default defineNuxtPlugin(async () => {
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100))
  useHead({
    title: `title after async`,
  })
})
```

This will throw an error:

> useHead() was called without provide context, ensure you call it through the setup() function.

The solution is twofold: 
1. We need an easy way for end users to import the head utils when auto-imports are disabled.
    -  The import is `#app/composables/head`
2. We need to replace or warn about `@unhead/vue` imports.
    - This is being handled by an Unplugin plugin

We avoid any extra aliasing as it creates more issues than it solves.

body:
Fixes another bullet point from #601, namely:

- use interpolation objects instead of `update_basin`, which still relies on time being sorted first

Now we can also use `parse_static_and_time` for Basin, bringing our node types more in line with each other and more code reuse.  For this I had to extend it a bit to support other interpolation types, and support IDs not being in time nor static. We still add time of new data as tstops to ensure the solver knows about net data as it happens.

Labeling this as breaking since before this we allowed a node ID to be in both the static and time tables. In `parse_static_and_time` (the other node types) we specifically check for this with a clear error message. I had to update `basic_transient`, to remove the static table there.

SonarQube analysis reported issues on the latest code changes. Even though this is not a required check, we should comply when the suggestions are sensible. Here's a link to the findings: https://sonarcloud.io/summary/new_code?id=dhis2_dashboard-app&branch=master

Summary of changes and the quality that was flagged by Sonarqube: 
* ActionsBar: break up nested ternary (maintainability)
* InformationBlock.module.css and SlideshowControlbar.module.css: missing generic font, but since this is declared higher up in the html structure for all elements (*), font-family declarations can be removed all-together in the app (reliability)
* NavigationMenu.js: remove role="listitem" on `li` element since it is is implicit (reliability, maintainability)
* ContentMenuItem.js: non-interactive element needs key handler. Fix was to make it semantically correct and switch to an interactive element `button` (reliability, maintainability)
* StartScreen.module.css: remove shorthand style that followed a more specific style (reliability)
* spec files - use object spread instead of Object.assign (conventional, maintainability)


What needs to be tested:
* start screen: that the bullets on the list of recent dashboards looks the same
* edit view item selector: that the launch link of each visualization looks the same and still works
* that the slideshow button has the correct tooltip content 
* InformationBlock and Slideshow controller have the correct font
* Dashboard dropdown "No dashboards found" looks correct
